title: Vela Art Co-op v. Ironworks Holdings: Hailstorm Structural Dispute
premise: An artist in a converted warehouse space in Austin, Texas, disputes the legality of their eviction, citing the landlord's negligence in maintaining structural integrity during a severe hailstorm.

side_A.role: an organiser with a tenants' union
side_A.goal: supporting the tenant against an unfair eviction

side_B.goal: justifying the eviction on grounds of lease violations

=== DOCUMENT 1: Incident and Maintenance Log – Ironworks Holdings Property Management ===

**Property ID:** IH-204-A (Vela Art Co-op Unit)
**Date Range:** January 1, 2024 – May 10, 2024
**Log Type:** Automated Maintenance & Communication Record

*Sender:* R. Alvarez, Certified Roof Inspector (Alvarez & Co. Inspections)
*Subject:* Routine Inspection Report – IH-204-A

=== DOCUMENT 2: Witness Statement – Elena Voss ===

**Statement of Elena Voss**
**Role:** Tenants' Union Organizer, Vela Art Co-op
**Date of Statement:** May 15, 2024

I have been the union organizer for the Vela Art Co-op tenants for three years. I know this building, and I know that the landlord, Ironworks Holdings, has been cutting corners on maintenance for years. Their property management company is based in Dallas, Texas, and they manage 50 other units in the state. They treat this building like a distant asset, not a home for artists.

The situation on May 2 was catastrophic, but it was entirely preventable. We are not just talking about a few drops of water. We are talking about a $120,000 investment in artistic equipment that was stored in the affected ground-floor area. That equipment is our livelihood. It is destroyed.

The roof membrane was visibly cracked and deteriorating weeks before the storm, making it unable to withstand standard hail. I saw it. I saw the black spots on the north-facing roof section where the granules had completely washed away. It wasn't just "minor granule loss" as the inspector’s letter might have vaguely suggested; it was structural decay. The landlord ignored our warnings.

Furthermore, the landlord received specific written notice of a leaking roof section on April 20, 2024, and failed to act. I sent that email. I pointed out the stains. I told them it was a leak. They ignored it. They claimed it was just "wear and tear," which is a lie. It was a breach of their contractual duty to maintain the roof to manufacturer standards.

The water entered through a pre-existing gap in the flashing, which was a known maintenance failure. I have photos of the gap from before the storm. It was wide enough to put a finger through. When the hail hit, the water didn't just drip; it poured through that gap because the flashing was already detached from the substrate.

Now, they are trying to evict us. The eviction notice was served on May 10, 2024, citing "failure to pay rent" as the primary reason. This is a pretext. The "failure to pay rent" claim was a pretext, as the tenant had already disputed the rent due to uninhabitable conditions. We did not pay the April rent because the space was not fit for purpose. The gallery space is located on the ground floor, directly beneath the disputed roof section. If the ceiling is dripping on your $120,000 of equipment, you cannot be expected to pay full rent for a hazardous environment.

We paid the full rent of $4,500 for April 2024 on time, via wire transfer. Wait, I need to clarify the dates. The lease started March 1. The April rent was due on May 1. We disputed it. But the May 10 eviction notice claims non-payment. This is illegal. The dispute over conditions does not constitute a valid legal defense to non-payment under the lease? That is what they say, but it is morally bankrupt. We are being punished for demanding a safe space.

The storm was severe. The National Weather Service measured hailstones at 1.5 inches in diameter. Yes, it was a bad storm. But a properly maintained roof should have held. The membrane was not in good condition. It was failing. And they left us to the mercy of the storm.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Witness Statement – Marcus Thorne ===

**Statement of Marcus Thorne**
**Role:** Landlord’s Counsel, Ironworks Holdings
**Date of Statement:** May 15, 2024

I represent Ironworks Holdings in this dispute. My client has always adhered to the terms of the lease agreement dated March 1, 2023, and applicable building codes. The local building code requires a minimum roof slope of 2:12 for standing seam metal in the area, and our roof meets this specification. The building was last renovated in 2019, at which time a new HVAC system was installed, ensuring the structure was updated to modern standards. The building's structural engineer certified the load-bearing walls as sound in 2022, which confirms the integrity of the underlying structure.

The events of May 2, 2024, were an Act of God. The hailstorm was of extreme severity. The National Weather Service confirmed hailstones at 1.5 inches in diameter. This is not standard hail; this is severe weather that exceeds the design limits of many commercial roofing systems.

The roof membrane was in good condition and fully compliant with standards prior to the storm; the damage was solely due to the severity of the hail. We have a certified inspector who issued a warning letter on January 15, 2024. The letter noted "minor granule loss" on the north-facing roof section. This is a normal aging process for asphalt-based membranes. It does not indicate structural failure or a breach of the manufacturer’s standards. The landlord’s maintenance log shows a roof inspection was performed on December 1, 2023, which found the roof to be in acceptable condition.

Regarding the notice of maintenance, no specific notice of a leak was received by the management company before the storm; the tenant only complained about general "wear and tear." The email from Ms. Voss on April 20, 2024, did not specify a leak. It mentioned "water spots" and "wear and tear." In the absence of a specific, verified report of a leak, our management team did not have the information to dispatch an emergency repair crew. The landlord's contract with the roof repair vendor includes a 48-hour response time for emergency calls, but this is triggered by a verified emergency, not a general complaint about stains.

The water entered through a puncture caused by a large hailstone that penetrated the intact membrane. The forensic analysis we have commissioned indicates that the entry point is a clean, circular puncture consistent with the impact of a 1.5-inch hailstone at high velocity. There is no evidence of a pre-existing gap in the flashing. The flashing was intact prior to the storm. The tenant’s claim that the water entered through a pre-existing gap is unfounded and contradicted by the physical evidence of the impact site.

Finally, regarding the eviction. The tenant’s security deposit of $9,000 is held in a segregated interest-bearing account, as required by law. The tenant’s rent was increased by 5% in the 2024 renewal, aligning with the Austin CPI, which is a standard market adjustment. The tenant failed to pay the full rent amount by the deadline, and the dispute over conditions does not constitute a valid legal defense to non-payment under the lease. The lease is clear: rent is due on the 1st. The tenant did not pay the full amount. The eviction notice served on May 10, 2024, is legally sound because the tenant is in breach of the primary financial obligation of the lease. The tenant’s artistic equipment, valued at $120,000, is covered by their own insurance policy, which covers interior damage up to $50,000, excluding structural failures. The tenant is responsible for their own business assets.

=== DOCUMENT 4: Email Correspondence – Vela Art Co-op to Ironworks Holdings ===

**From:** elena.voss@velaartcoop.org
**To:** management@ironworksholdings.com
**Date:** May 4, 2024, 09:15 AM
**Subject:** URGENT: Emergency Repair Quote Needed – IH-204-A

To the Property Management Team,

I am writing to formally request an emergency repair quote for the roof damage sustained during the hailstorm on May 2, 2024.

As you are aware, the hailstorm was severe, with NWS reporting 1.5-inch hailstones. The impact has resulted in significant water ingress into the building. Specifically, the water is entering the ground floor gallery space, which is located directly beneath the north-facing roof section.

This area contains sensitive artistic equipment and artwork. We are facing immediate risk of further damage. We request that you contact your roof repair vendor immediately to provide a quote for emergency stabilization and repair.

We note that your contract with the roof repair vendor includes a 48-hour response time for emergency calls. Given the ongoing nature of the water damage, we consider this an emergency.

We also remind you that the lease agreement stipulates that the landlord is responsible for maintaining the roof membrane to manufacturer standards. The current state of the roof, following the storm, is a failure of that standard.

We expect a response within 24 hours.

Sincerely,

Elena Voss
Tenants' Union Organizer
Vela Art Co-op

**---**

**From:** management@ironworksholdings.com
**To:** elena.voss@velaartcoop.org
**Date:** May 4, 2024, 02:30 PM
**Subject:** RE: URGENT: Emergency Repair Quote Needed – IH-204-A

Dear Ms. Voss,

We have received your email regarding the roof damage. Please be advised that we are currently reviewing the incident with our insurance carrier and the roof repair vendor.

We have noted your request for a quote. Please understand that emergency response protocols are activated based on verified structural emergencies. We are gathering data from the storm event and the condition of the roof prior to the event.

Regarding the rent, please note that the April 2024 rent payment was not received in full. The lease requires timely payment of the full amount. The dispute over the condition of the roof does not relieve you of the obligation to pay rent. We will be sending a notice regarding the unpaid balance shortly.

We will follow up with the vendor’s assessment once available.

Sincerely,

Ironworks Holdings Property Management
Dallas, TX
